_about: Hand-authored, client-facing summaries for every service and action. Merged over documentation.json by tools/genmodel.py - the analysis fields remain the ground truth; this layer explains the wire contract to someone implementing a client. Keys: service = control path, action = action name.

/AlarmClock/Control.summary: Alarm scheduler for the zone. Lets a client create, list, update and delete alarms, and read/set the household clock settings those alarms run against (current time, time zone, time server, 12/24h and date formats, and the daily music-index refresh time). Alarms target a single room by UUID and can play a stream URI or a library playlist at a fixed volume, optionally grouping linked zones. Changes are announced through the evented AlarmListVersion.

actions.CreateAlarm: Creates a new alarm and returns its AssignedID, which is needed for UpdateAlarm and DestroyAlarm. StartLocalTime and Duration use 'HH:MM:SS'; Recurrence is a keyword such as ONCE, EVERYDAY, WEEKDAYS or WEEKENDS. RoomUUID selects the player, ProgramURI/ProgramMetaData choose what plays (a stream URI, or a Sonos playlist/library URI), PlayMode picks e.g. NORMAL or SHUFFLE_NOREPEAT, Volume is 0-100, and IncludeLinkedZones controls whether bonded players join in.
actions.DestroyAlarm: Deletes the alarm with the given ID (an AssignedID previously returned by CreateAlarm, or an id from ListAlarms). Returns nothing; the change shows up in AlarmListVersion.
actions.GetDailyIndexRefreshTime: Returns the 'HH:MM:SS' local time at which the player rebuilds the local music-library index each day.
actions.GetFormat: Returns the player's time and date display preferences (e.g. 12h vs 24h clock).
actions.GetHouseholdTimeAtStamp: Converts a monotonically-increasing household timestamp (as used in event and queue bookkeeping) into an absolute UTC time.
actions.GetTimeNow: Returns the player's current UTC time, local time, time zone and TimeGeneration (a counter that increments whenever the household clock is set - useful for detecting clock changes).
actions.GetTimeServer: Returns the configured household time-server address used to keep zone clocks in sync.
actions.GetTimeZone: Returns the current time zone index and whether DST is auto-adjusted. Use GetTimeZoneRule to resolve the index to a tz rule string.
actions.GetTimeZoneAndRule: Same as GetTimeZone but also returns the resolved CurrentTimeZone rule string in one call.
actions.GetTimeZoneRule: Looks up a time zone rule string (POSIX-style TZ spec) by Index.
actions.ListAlarms: Returns the full alarm list as an XML document plus CurrentAlarmListVersion. The version counter is the cheap way to poll for changes; it is also evented.
actions.SetDailyIndexRefreshTime: Changes the daily library-index refresh time ('HH:MM:SS').
actions.SetFormat: Sets the 12/24-hour time format and the date format.
actions.SetTimeNow: Sets the player's clock: DesiredTime is UTC 'HH:MM:SS'-style time plus a time zone so the local offset can be derived. Setting the clock bumps TimeGeneration.
actions.SetTimeServer: Sets the address of the household time server (host/IP used for clock sync).
actions.SetTimeZone: Selects the time zone by Index and toggles automatic DST adjustment.
actions.UpdateAlarm: Edits an existing alarm in place. ID is the AssignedID from CreateAlarm or ListAlarms; the remaining arguments carry the complete replacement definition (same fields as CreateAlarm), so callers should send the full record rather than a diff.

/AudioIn/Control.summary: The legacy hardware line-in service. Its SCPD (AudioIn1.xml) still ships and its route is still registered, but the service is not listed in the device description and every action dispatches to a stub that unconditionally faults 401. The feature was removed on this model; treat all six actions as dead surface - documented here so clients can recognise the fault. The actions below describe what the API used to do.

actions.StartTransmissionToGroup: Historically started streaming this player's analog line-in to the group identified by CoordinatorID, returning the resulting transport settings. In this build it always faults 401.
actions.StopTransmissionToGroup: Historically stopped line-in transmission to the group. In this build it always faults 401.
actions.SetAudioInputAttributes: Historically renamed the line-in source and set its icon. In this build it always faults 401.
actions.GetAudioInputAttributes: Historically returned the line-in source name and icon. In this build it always faults 401.
actions.SetLineInLevel: Historically set left/right line-in gain levels. In this build it always faults 401.
actions.GetLineInLevel: Historically returned the left/right line-in gain levels. In this build it always faults 401.

/DeviceProperties/Control.summary: Player identity, hardware features and local configuration: zone name/icon, serial/software/hardware versions, LED and button state, button lock, autoplay preferences (which room's line-in or TV input auto-plays here and at what volume), stereo-pair and home-theater satellite management, household id, config mode, and the room-detection chirp used during setup.

actions.AddBondedZones: Bonds additional players to this player via a ChannelMapSet (which member plays which channel).
actions.AddHTSatellite: Adds a surround/sub satellite to a home-theater group via HTSatChanMapSet.
actions.CreateStereoPair: Creates a stereo pair from two players, describing left/right assignment in ChannelMapSet.
actions.EnterConfigMode: Puts the player into a configuration mode (used during setup/registration); returns the resulting State.
actions.GetAutoplayLinkedZones: For a given autoplay Source, returns whether linked zones are grouped when autoplay triggers.
actions.GetAutoplayRoomUUID: For a given autoplay Source, returns the UUID of the room that will take over playback.
actions.GetAutoplayVolume: Returns the volume the player jumps to when the given autoplay Source activates.
actions.GetButtonLockState: Returns whether the player's physical buttons are locked (child-lock).
actions.GetButtonState: Returns the current physical button state (e.g. which buttons are pressed).
actions.GetHouseholdID: Returns the household identifier this player is registered to.
actions.GetLEDState: Returns whether the status LED is on or off.
actions.GetUseAutoplayVolume: Returns whether autoplay applies the configured autoplay volume (vs. keeping current volume).
actions.GetZoneAttributes: Returns the player's configured room name, icon and room configuration.
actions.GetZoneInfo: Returns identity and version info: serial number, software/hardware versions, IP and MAC addresses, flags and build metadata.
actions.RemoveBondedZones: Un-bonds zones described by ChannelMapSet; KeepGrouped controls whether playback grouping is preserved.
actions.RemoveHTSatellite: Removes a home-theater satellite by room UUID.
actions.RoomDetectionStartChirping: Plays the ultrasonic chirp used by Sonos room/speaker detection during setup; returns a PlayId to stop it.
actions.RoomDetectionStopChirping: Stops a chirp previously started by RoomDetectionStartChirping.
actions.SeparateStereoPair: Breaks a stereo pair described by ChannelMapSet back into two independent players.
actions.SetAutoplayLinkedZones: Sets whether autoplay groups linked zones for a Source.
actions.SetAutoplayRoomUUID: Sets which room UUID autoplay for a Source should target.
actions.SetAutoplayVolume: Sets the autoplay volume for a Source.
actions.SetButtonLockState: Locks or unlocks the player's physical buttons.
actions.SetLEDState: Turns the status LED on or off.
actions.SetUseAutoplayVolume: Enables or disables applying the autoplay volume.
actions.SetZoneAttributes: Sets the room name, icon and configuration shown to users.

/GroupManagement/Control.summary: Coordinator-facing group-membership service. Group members use these actions to join/leave a coordinator and to report buffering state; normal clients rarely call it, but it is advertised. Everything here operates on group members identified by MemberID.

actions.AddMember: Joins the calling member (MemberID + BootSeq) to this group. Returns the coordinator's current URI, the joined group UUID, volume/reset hints and transport settings so the new member can align playback.
actions.ReportTrackBufferingResult: Member-to-coordinator feedback of a buffering ResultCode for a track fetch. NOTE: the implementation unconditionally returns 402 in this build - effectively a non-functional stub.
actions.SetSourceAreaIds: Sets the group's desired source-area ids (used to steer which zone's content the group plays).

/HTControl/Control.summary: Home-theater control: IR repeater passthrough, LED feedback, and IR-remote learning so a TV remote can drive volume on the soundbar. Relevant to playbar-family hardware with an IR receiver.

actions.CommitLearnedIRCodes: Stores the codes captured by LearnIRCode under a remote Name.
actions.GetIRRepeaterState: Returns whether IR commands are retransmitted to the AV equipment.
actions.GetLEDFeedbackState: Returns the LED feedback state used to acknowledge IR-learned volume presses.
actions.IdentifyIRRemote: Asks the user to press buttons so the player can identify the remote layout, bounded by Timeout (seconds).
actions.IsRemoteConfigured: Returns whether an IR remote has been configured.
actions.LearnIRCode: Captures a single IRCode within Timeout during remote setup.
actions.SetIRRepeaterState: Enables or disables IR repeater passthrough.
actions.SetLEDFeedbackState: Sets the LED feedback pattern for IR volume presses.

/MediaRenderer/AVTransport/Control.summary: The playback engine of the zone - the largest service. Covers transport control (Play/Pause/Stop/Next/Previous), seeking, source selection via URIs and metadata, play modes and crossfade, the implicit playback queue (add/remove/reorder/clear), saved queues, group coordination transfer (one player handing the coordinator role to another, with full state snapshots), alarms/sleep timers, and Sonos-specific extras like autoplay and direct-control sessions. InstanceID is always 0. Many mutating actions take UpdateID for optimistic concurrency: pass the last queue UpdateID you saw and the call fails if the queue changed underneath you.

actions.AddMultipleURIsToQueue: Bulk-enqueues tracks into the implicit playback queue. EnqueuedURIs and EnqueuedURIMetaData are parallel lists (count must equal NumberOfURIs); DesiredFirstTrackNumberEnqueued positions them, EnqueueAsNext inserts after the current track. ContainerURI/ContainerMetaData describe the source list itself. UpdateID guards against concurrent queue edits. Returns where the tracks landed, how many were added, and the new length/UpdateID.
actions.AddURIToQueue: Adds one track URI (+DIDL-Lite metadata) to the playback queue. DesiredFirstTrackNumberEnqueued picks the position (0 = append), EnqueueAsNext inserts right after the current track. Returns the 1-based position where it landed and tracks actually added.
actions.AddURIToSavedQueue: Adds a track to a saved queue identified by ObjectID at AddAtIndex. Returns counts and a NewUpdateID for that queue.
actions.BackupQueue: Persists the current playback queue to flash so it survives reboot.
actions.BecomeCoordinatorOfStandaloneGroup: Makes this player coordinate the standalone group it belongs to; returns the coordinator id and new group id. Used in group rebuild flows.
actions.BecomeGroupCoordinator: Bulk state-transfer: this player takes over as group coordinator, receiving the previous coordinator's complete transport/queue/alarm/sleep state in the arguments (TransportSettings, CurrentQueueTrackList, member list, etc.). Nothing is read from arg descriptors - the handler forwards the whole blob.
actions.BecomeGroupCoordinatorAndSource: Like BecomeGroupCoordinator but also transfers the audio source state (CurrentAVTTrackList, CurrentSourceState, ResumePlayback flag) so the new coordinator continues the same source.
actions.ChangeCoordinator: Asks this coordinator to hand coordination to NewCoordinator, carrying the current transport settings and URI so playback continues; RestartSink controls whether the sink restarts.
actions.ChangeTransportSettings: Applies a new TransportSettings blob (play state, mode, etc.) to the current URI - used when a group coordinator pushes state to members.
actions.ConfigureSleepTimer: Sets a sleep timer that fades playback out after NewSleepTimerDuration ('HH:MM:SS').
actions.CreateSavedQueue: Creates a new named saved queue containing one initial track (EnqueuedURI + metadata) and returns its AssignedObjectID plus queue stats.
actions.DelegateGroupCoordinationTo: Hands the coordinator role to NewCoordinator. RejoinGroup controls whether this player stays as a member; ClearSource (added in 86.10) controls whether it drops the source.
actions.EndDirectControlSession: Ends a cloud/direct-control playback session, returning the player to normal UPnP control.
actions.GetCrossfadeMode: Returns whether crossfade between tracks is enabled.
actions.GetCurrentTransportActions: Returns the actions currently legal for this source as a CSV (e.g. 'Play,Pause,Stop,Seek') - depends on the stream type and capabilities, so poll it rather than assuming.
actions.GetDeviceCapabilities: Returns what media this player can play/record and its recording quality modes.
actions.GetMediaInfo: Returns metadata about the current media source: track count and duration, current/next URIs + metadata, and the medium (queue, stream, line-in) - i.e. what container is loaded rather than where playback is within it (use GetPositionInfo for that).
actions.GetPositionInfo: Returns where playback sits inside the media: current track number/URI/metadata, track duration, relative and absolute position times, and track counts.
actions.GetRemainingSleepTimerDuration: Returns the time left on the sleep timer and the timer generation counter.
actions.GetRunningAlarmProperties: If an alarm is currently ringing, returns its ID, group and the logged start time.
actions.GetTransportInfo: Returns transport state (PLAYING/PAUSED_PLAYBACK/STOPPED/TRANSITIONING), status and speed.
actions.GetTransportSettings: Returns the current play mode (NORMAL/REPEAT_ALL/SHUFFLE…) and recording quality mode.
actions.Next: Skips to the next track in the queue. Faults (typically 711/701 family) if the current source doesn't support skipping.
actions.NotifyDeletedURI: Tells the player a URI it may have queued has been deleted from the server so it can drop or skip it.
actions.Pause: Pauses playback. Only valid while playing; faults on sources that can't pause.
actions.Play: Starts or resumes playback. Speed selects the rate - '1' is normal; fractional rate strings select slower/faster trick-play on sources that support it.
actions.Previous: Skips back to the previous track.
actions.RemoveAllTracksFromQueue: Clears the implicit playback queue entirely.
actions.RemoveTrackFromQueue: Removes the queued track identified by ObjectID (track object id), guarded by UpdateID for optimistic concurrency.
actions.RemoveTrackRangeFromQueue: Removes NumberOfTracks consecutive tracks starting at 1-based StartingIndex; returns the NewUpdateID.
actions.ReorderTracksInQueue: Moves a run of tracks (StartingIndex + NumberOfTracks) to InsertBefore within the queue, UpdateID-guarded.
actions.ReorderTracksInSavedQueue: Rewrites a saved queue's ordering from TrackList/NewPositionList; returns length change and new UpdateID.
actions.RunAlarm: Server-driven 'fire this alarm now' trigger carrying the full alarm definition - used internally when an alarm goes off; also useful for testing alarm playback.
actions.SaveQueue: Saves the current playback queue as a named saved queue (Title); ObjectID selects an existing saved queue to overwrite. Returns AssignedObjectID.
actions.Seek: Repositions playback. Unit selects the seek mode: TRACK_NR jumps to a track number, REL_TIME seeks to 'HH:MM:SS' from track start, TIME_DELTA does a relative jump. Parsing is lenient (numeric prefixes accepted, trailing junk ignored) but the accepted Unit set and the semantics depend on whether the source is indexed or streamed - a request can be accepted yet ignored downstream, so check GetPositionInfo after seeking.
actions.SetAVTransportURI: Loads a new source: a track/stream URI plus its DIDL-Lite metadata. This is how a client starts a radio stream or a file URI - the previous queue position is not implied; you typically call Play afterwards.
actions.SetNextAVTransportURI: Sets up gapless playback: the URI + metadata that should follow the current track, so the decoder can pre-buffer it.
actions.SetPlayMode: Sets play mode: NORMAL, REPEAT_ALL, REPEAT_ONE, SHUFFLE, SHUFFLE_NOREPEAT, SHUFFLE_REPEAT_ONE (exact accepted set is enforced).
actions.SnoozeAlarm: Snoozes the currently ringing alarm by Duration ('HH:MM:SS').
actions.StartAutoplay: Starts autoplay for a source: plays ProgramURI (+metadata) at the configured autoplay volume, optionally grouping linked zones; ResetVolumeAfter restores volume afterwards.
actions.Stop: Stops playback and clears transport position.

/MediaRenderer/ConnectionManager/Control.summary: Standard UPnP ConnectionManager for the renderer half of the device. On Sonos this is mostly vestigial (playback isn't pull-pushed through UPnP connections), so connection ids are typically empty - but the three actions are the real spec.

actions.GetCurrentConnectionIDs: Returns the CSV list of active connection ids (usually empty on a zone player).
actions.GetCurrentConnectionInfo: Returns per-connection detail (peer manager, protocol info, direction, status) for a ConnectionID previously returned by GetCurrentConnectionIDs.
actions.GetProtocolInfo: Returns the Source and Sink protocol-info CSVs - the MIME-type/protocol strings this renderer can play.

/MediaRenderer/GroupRenderingControl/Con.summary: Group-level volume control. These actions apply to the whole group coordinated by this player - SetGroupVolume applies the same absolute volume to every member, while SetRelativeGroupVolume keeps the members' relative offsets (that's the action Sonos apps call for the group volume slider). SnapshotGroupVolume exists so a ramp/group adjustment can later be balanced.

actions.GetGroupMute: Returns the group mute state (any/all-muted semantics per the coordinator).
actions.SetGroupMute: Mutes or unmutes every player in the group.
actions.SetGroupVolume: Sets every member of the group to the same absolute DesiredVolume (0-100).
actions.SetRelativeGroupVolume: Adjusts group volume by a signed Adjustment while preserving per-player offsets; returns the resulting NewVolume. Prefer this over SetGroupVolume for slider UIs.
actions.SnapshotGroupVolume: Captures per-member volumes so a subsequent group adjustment can be made consistently.

/MediaRenderer/Queue/Control.summary: The multi-queue registry: explicit saved/independent queues addressed by QueueID, separate from the implicit playback queue AVTransport edits. Provides create/attach/browse/mutate operations with optimistic concurrency - every mutating action takes the queue's last UpdateID and returns the new one, and a stale UpdateID faults. AttachQueue is how a client adopts a queue owned by another context.

actions.AddMultipleURIs: Bulk-adds tracks to an explicit queue: EnqueuedURIsAndMetaData holds NumberOfURIs packed URI+metadata entries; positioning via DesiredFirstTrackNumberEnqueued or EnqueueAsNext. UpdateID-guarded.
actions.AddURI: Adds a single track (+DIDL-Lite metadata) to the queue at DesiredFirstTrackNumberEnqueued (or after the current track with EnqueueAsNext). Returns its position, count added and the new UpdateID.
actions.AttachQueue: Attaches to a queue owned by QueueOwnerID, returning the QueueID to use in subsequent calls plus the owner context.
actions.Backup: Persists the queue registry to flash (trackqueue.rsq) so queues survive reboot.
actions.Browse: Reads back a queue's contents: starting at StartingIndex, up to RequestedCount tracks, returned as a DIDL-Lite Result document with NumberReturned/TotalMatches and the queue's UpdateID.
actions.CreateQueue: Creates a new queue owned by QueueOwnerID with a policy (QueuePolicy), returning its QueueID.
actions.RemoveTrackRange: Removes NumberOfTracks consecutive tracks starting at StartingIndex; returns NewUpdateID.
actions.ReorderTracks: Moves a run of tracks to InsertBefore within the queue; UpdateID-guarded.
actions.ReplaceAllTracks: Atomically replaces the whole queue contents: new tracks from ContainerURI/ContainerMetaData plus packed EnqueuedURIsAndMetaData, with CurrentTrackIndex/NewCurrentTrackIndices pointing at what should be playing. Bulk transfer - no per-arg capacity limits.
actions.SaveAsSonosPlaylist: Saves the queue as a Sonos playlist (Title); ObjectID selects an existing playlist to overwrite. Returns AssignedObjectID.

/MediaRenderer/RenderingControl/Control.summary: Per-player audio rendering: volume (linear 0-100 and dB), mute, bass/treble/loudness and extended EQ, fixed (line-out level) output mode, headphone detection, room-calibration enable, and volume ramps used by alarms/sleep timers. Channel is 'Master' or 'LF'/'RF' for stereo pairs. NOTE: several actions are deliberately neutered on this hardware (e.g. GetBass is a confirmed no-op) - check each action's status before trusting it.

actions.GetBass: Returns bass level - BUT it is neutered on this build: the implementation is a confirmed no-op stub, so the returned CurrentBass is meaningless. GetEQ(EQType='Bass') is the working path.
actions.GetEQ: Reads an EQ parameter by EQType (e.g. Bass/Treble/Loudness-style ids) from the audio pipeline.
actions.GetHeadphoneConnected: Returns whether headphones are plugged in (players with a headphone jack).
actions.GetLoudness: Returns the loudness-compensation setting for a Channel.
actions.GetMute: Returns mute state for a Channel ('Master' unless addressing a stereo-pair side).
actions.GetOutputFixed: Returns whether output is at fixed level (for line-out/receiver use) vs. variable.
actions.GetRoomCalibrationStatus: Returns whether room calibration (Trueplay) is enabled and available on this player.
actions.GetSupportsOutputFixed: Returns whether this hardware supports fixed-level output mode at all.
actions.GetTreble: Returns treble level - same neutering caveat as GetBass may apply; GetEQ is the reliable path.
actions.GetVolume: Returns the linear volume for a Channel (0-100).
actions.GetVolumeDB: Returns the volume in decibels (scaled; see GetVolumeDBRange for this player's range).
actions.GetVolumeDBRange: Returns the dB volume range this player supports.
actions.RampToVolume: Starts a timed volume ramp to DesiredVolume of type RampType (used for alarm/sleep-timer fades); returns RampTime.
actions.ResetBasicEQ: Resets bass/treble/loudness and stereo balance to neutral; returns the resulting values.
actions.ResetExtEQ: Resets the extended EQ band EQType.
actions.RestoreVolumePriorToRamp: Undoes a previous RampToVolume, restoring the earlier volume.
actions.SetBass: Sets the bass level - neutered like GetBass on this build; use SetEQ with the bass EQType instead.
actions.SetChannelMap: Assigns left/right channels to players in a stereo pair via ChannelMap.
actions.SetEQ: Sets an EQ parameter (EQType, e.g. bass/treble/loudness id) to DesiredValue - the working EQ path.
actions.SetLoudness: Enables or disables loudness compensation for a Channel.
actions.SetOutputFixed: Switches between fixed and variable output level where supported.
actions.SetRelativeVolume: Adjusts volume by a signed Adjustment; returns NewVolume. Safer than absolute SetVolume for slider deltas.
actions.SetRoomCalibrationStatus: Enables or disables Trueplay room calibration.
actions.SetTreble: Sets treble level - same neuter caveat; prefer SetEQ.
actions.SetVolume: Sets the linear volume for a Channel (0-100).
actions.SetVolumeDB: Sets the volume in decibels within the range reported by GetVolumeDBRange.

/MediaRenderer/VirtualLineIn/Control.summary: Treats a networked line-in source as a virtual transport on this player - transport-style control (Play/Pause/Stop/Next/Previous/SetVolume) plus Start/StopTransmission to run the session. It's the 'line-in from another player' surface.

actions.Play: Starts/resumes the virtual line-in source at the given Speed ('1' normal).
actions.Previous: Steps the virtual line-in transport back.
actions.SetVolume: Sets the playback volume for the line-in session.
actions.StartTransmission: Begins receiving the line-in stream from the given CoordinatorID; returns the resulting transport settings.
actions.StopTransmission: Ends the line-in transmission from the given coordinator.

/MediaServer/ConnectionManager/Control.summary: Standard UPnP ConnectionManager for the embedded MediaServer (the side that serves the local library). Same three actions as the renderer variant.

actions.GetCurrentConnectionIDs: Returns the CSV list of active connection ids (normally empty).
actions.GetCurrentConnectionInfo: Returns per-connection detail for the media-server side. Unlike the renderer twin it takes no ConnectionID argument and reports the single active/default connection.
actions.GetProtocolInfo: Returns the Source/Sink protocol-info CSVs the media server supports.

/MediaServer/ContentDirectory/Control.summary: The local music-library service. Browse is the workhorse: hierarchical object ids (folders, artists, albums, playlists, shares) returning DIDL-Lite XML with paging via StartingIndex/RequestedCount and change detection via UpdateID/GetSystemUpdateID. Also covers object create/update/delete for editable containers, prefix lookups used by the app, share-index refresh control, and sort/browse capability queries. NOTE: the Search action is gone in this build - it exists in 25.2-era firmware but has been removed here.

actions.Browse: Browses the library tree. ObjectID selects the container (e.g. 'Q:0' the queue, 'A:ARTIST', 'SQ:' saved queues, 'S:' shares, music-service object ids); BrowseFlag is BrowseDirectChildren or BrowseMetadata; Filter/SortCriteria follow the CDS spec. Returns DIDL-Lite Result, counts, and an UpdateID that changes when the container does - cache on it.
actions.CreateObject: Creates an object (e.g. a playlist entry) inside ContainerID; Elements is a DIDL-Lite fragment. Returns the new ObjectID.
actions.FindPrefix: Locates the object prefix for ObjectID - returns the StartingIndex under the given Prefix and an UpdateID (used to map an item back to its container position).
actions.GetAlbumArtistDisplayOption: Returns whether the library groups by album artist or contributing artist.
actions.GetAllPrefixLocations: Returns all container prefixes that contain ObjectID (an item can live under several indices).
actions.GetBrowseable: Returns whether the local library share is currently marked browseable.
actions.GetLastIndexChange: Returns the timestamp/id of the last library reindex - cheap polling point for 'did the library change'.
actions.GetSearchCapabilities: Returns which DIDL properties Search would accept - vestigial since Search itself is removed in this build.
actions.GetShareIndexInProgress: Returns whether a library reindex is currently running.
actions.GetSortCapabilities: Returns which DIDL properties can be used in Browse SortCriteria.
actions.GetSystemUpdateID: Returns the global library UpdateID - compare before/after to detect any change.
actions.RefreshShareIndex: Triggers a rescan of the configured music shares.
actions.RequestResort: Re-sorts the library index using SortOrder.
actions.SetBrowseable: Marks the library share browseable or not.
actions.UpdateObject: Rewrites an object's metadata: CurrentTagValue -> NewTagValue DIDL fragments for ObjectID.

/MusicServices/Control.summary: SMAPI music-service discovery: which streaming services are configured on the household and their descriptor metadata (capabilities, auth type, presentation maps). The account credentials themselves live under SystemProperties.

actions.GetSessionId: Returns the session id used to authenticate SMAPI calls for the given ServiceId + Username.
actions.ListAvailableServices: Returns the full music-service descriptor list (XML: service ids, names, capabilities, auth policies, presentation metadata) plus the flat type list and a version counter for change detection.
actions.UpdateAvailableServices: Forces a refresh of the cached service descriptor list from the cloud/catalog.

/QPlay/Control.summary: Tencent QPlay handshake - the single-action auth protocol used by QQ Music clients on Chinese-market zones. The device description advertises QPlay:2 capability via qq:X_QPlay_SoftwareCapability rather than a serviceType.

actions.QPlayAuth: Auth exchange: client sends a Seed string; the player returns Code, MID and DID used to derive the session key. Faults if the seed doesn't decode.

/SystemProperties/Control.summary: A generic key/value store plus the music-service account manager. SetString/GetString/Remove are a free-form property bag that many features lean on (client-facing settings ride through it). The account actions manage per-service credentials: legacy login (AddAccountX), OAuth (AddOAuthAccountX and friends keyed by AccountUDN), nickname/edit/remove, and credential refresh. Two SCPD-advertised actions are dead in this build: ProvisionCredentialedTrialAccountX (name string absent - hard-removed) and ResetThirdPartyCredentials (string present but unreferenced - soft-removed); both fault 401 on the wire.

actions.AddAccountX: Registers a music-service account with legacy credentials (AccountType id, AccountID username, AccountPassword); returns the AccountUDN used by all other account actions.
actions.AddOAuthAccountX: Registers an OAuth music-service account: AccountType plus token/key/device-id/authorization-code/redirect metadata and optional UserIdHashCode/AccountTier. Returns AccountUDN and the service-provided AccountNickname.
actions.DoPostUpdateTasks: Runs bookkeeping that should execute after a firmware update (data migration, cached-state rebuild).
actions.EditAccountMd: Replaces the metadata (Md) blob for an account.
actions.EditAccountPasswordX: Changes the password on a legacy-credential account.
actions.EnableRDM: Enables or disables Retail Demo Mode on the player.
actions.GetRDM: Returns whether Retail Demo Mode is enabled.
actions.GetString: Reads a property value by VariableName from the key/value store.
actions.GetWebCode: Returns a short WebCode for the given AccountType - used to link an account via the provider's web flow.
actions.RefreshAccountCredentialsX: Refreshes OAuth credentials (token/key) for an existing AccountUID.
actions.Remove: Deletes VariableName from the key/value store.
actions.RemoveAccount: Deletes a music-service account by AccountType + AccountID.
actions.ReplaceAccountX: Swaps the account behind AccountUDN for new credentials (NewAccountID/password or OAuth token set), returning NewAccountUDN.
actions.SetAccountNicknameX: Sets the display nickname for an AccountUDN.
actions.SetString: Writes VariableName=StringValue into the property store.

/ZoneGroupTopology/Control.summary: Zone topology and household management. GetZoneGroupState is the famous one: a single XML snapshot listing every group, member, coordinator and source - the fastest way to map a household. The rest covers software update control, mobile-device registration, diagnostics upload and coordinator callbacks for alarms/unresponsive members.

actions.BeginSoftwareUpdate: Starts a firmware update: UpdateURL to fetch from, Flags controlling behaviour (e.g. forced downgrade), ExtraOptions for transport options.
actions.CheckForUpdate: Asks whether a firmware update is available; UpdateType selects the channel, CachedOnly avoids the network fetch, Version filters; returns the UpdateItem XML.
actions.GetZoneGroupAttributes: Returns the household's group name/id, the member UUIDs, and the Muse household id.
actions.GetZoneGroupState: Returns the complete zone topology as an XML document: every group, its coordinator, member players, and what each is playing. The single most useful call for mapping a household.
actions.RegisterMobileDevice: Registers a mobile controller (name, UDN, IP:port) so the zone can push callbacks to it.
actions.ReportAlarmStartedRunning: Member-to-coordinator callback: reports that an alarm started running (drives 'alarm is playing' indicators).
actions.ReportUnresponsiveDevice: Reports a missing/unresponsive DeviceUUID with a DesiredAction (e.g. remove it from groups) so the coordinator can heal topology.
actions.SubmitDiagnostics: Uploads a diagnostics bundle; IncludeControllers widens scope, Type selects the dump kind; returns a DiagnosticID to quote to support.

subsystems.ab_experiments: Sonos can enrol a zone in A/B experiments pushed from the cloud. Each experiment is an id+name with a value and a shipped defaultValue, so a player without an assignment just runs the default. The /experiments HTTP endpoint exposes the active set. Client authors only need to know these exist — they change behaviour silently between households and explain builds that differ despite identical firmware.
subsystems.account_cert_lifecycle: Every player holds a device certificate used to authenticate to Sonos cloud and to music services that demand deviceCerts. The enrolment, renewal and storage flow lives here; when a client hits certificate errors (R_CLIENT_KEYCERT_* family) this is the machinery involved.
subsystems.audio_taps: Internal PCM capture points let the firmware record the audio passing through it — used for diagnostics and, importantly, for TV lip-sync: the SPDIF tap captures the TV input so playback can be synchronized against the output tap. The /snapshotspdiftap + /downloadspdiftap endpoints retrieve captures. Not a client-facing feature, but it explains audio-quality and latency behaviour on home-theatre setups.
subsystems.business_msp: Hooks for Sonos Business managed deployments — the strings reference adding/removing and syncing a 'Sonos Business MSP' relationship. Households under business management can have different service availability (e.g. Sonos Radio suppressed by the SBiz entitlement). Only vocabulary has been recovered.
subsystems.buttons_ir: Physical input pipeline. Buttons (play/pause, volume, join, mic-mute, pairing, plus swipe gestures on touch models) are broadcast on an internal multicast group and forwarded to the group coordinator when a player is slaved. Button lock is controllable via SOAP, and the cloud can inject virtual button presses (virtualRemoteControl/buttonCommand) — that's how the app 'remote control' works. IR: the player learns your TV remote via LearnIRCode against Sonos's ir.ws.sonos.com code database.
subsystems.chirp_stack: The embedded Chirp acoustic library — the speaker can literally emit and decode data-over-sound chirps (CDMA/FSK profiles). Used for room detection during setup and possibly trueplay discovery. Only the codec vocabulary is catalogued; the wire format hasn't been decoded.
subsystems.cloud_queue: Sonos's cloud-side queue: playbackMetadata/ratings, trackQueueAdditions and CloudQueueHistory all point at a queue that lives cloud-side rather than in trackqueue.rsq — this is how cloud services (e.g. voice assistants, direct control) schedule tracks. Ratings are explicitly 'only implemented for cloud queue'. The lifecycle and reconciliation with the local queue are not yet decoded.
subsystems.dsp_ht_engine: The full home-theatre audio configuration surface: surround/subwoofer state, downmix mode, dialog enhancement, AI speech enhancement, height-channel level, autoplay/autostop silence thresholds and a Tweaks bitmask — plus a 37-field per-zone audio record covering everything from balance and sub crossover to trueplay status. Channel masks up to 9.1.4 are compiled in. Many of these knobs are reachable through hidden RenderingControl EQ-type tokens (SubGain, SubCrossover, SpeakerSize, FV*...).
subsystems.embedded_sqlite: A libsqlite3 is linked in; at least the local timer/alarm store persists through SQL statements. Which tables exist and where the database file lives is still unmapped.
subsystems.entitlements: Sonos-side licensing: each account/household can carry <Entitlement> records (type, isTrial, sku, date range, codes). The runtime policy consults them — e.g. a Sonos Business (SBiz) entitlement blocks Sonos Radio preinstall. Changes fire entitlements_changed events. Fetched cloud-side, cached locally, and diffed on refresh.
subsystems.factory_reset: The wipe path: a factoryReset.txt sentinel file, sonosFactoryResetFull entry, LED_MODE_FACTORY_RESET feedback, and a remote management/factoryReset muse route. Steps and what survives (registration? certs?) are not yet decoded.
subsystems.favourites_model: Sonos Favourites (the pinned items in the app). They live in a replicated XML store (<Favorites SchemaVersion NextFavorite>) with a sibling <Radio> section for stations; ContentDirectory projects them as the FV:2 container whose changes bump FavoritesUpdateID. You create/delete/edit them through the normal CDS CreateObject/DestroyObject/UpdateObject actions against the favourites directory object, and the cloud mirrors them via the households/groups favorites routes. Radio favourites sit under the R: prefix instead.
subsystems.feature_flag_registry: Feature flags arrive as JSON keys in the cloud-delivered settings document — not compile-time switches. Ten featureConfig* keys enumerate what's gated (SemiSleep, SmartPlay, SpotABR, Plink, Quickbonding, MetricsService...). Explains behaviour that differs between households on the same firmware.
subsystems.group_object_model: How zones actually group: the coordinator/satellite topology, zone storage, play-state manager and the ZoneGroupTopology event model sit here. This is the machinery behind ZoneGroupState and the zgt events clients already consume.
subsystems.ibt_plans: An 'IBT' command-plan executor ('executing ibt plan for command') gated by the enablePitchfork feature flag — likely in-band tuning/test command plans. Almost nothing decoded.
subsystems.lechmere_wss: The persistent secure-websocket channel between player and cloud ('lechmere'): RFC6455 framing carrying an inner TLV command vocabulary — this is how the cloud pushes control and the player reports state in real time. Framing is confirmed; the per-namespace command payloads aren't decoded yet.
subsystems.led_engine: The status LED is a scripted animation system: patterns are programs of RGB steps with hold/fade times, checksummed and selected by internal state codes (R_LED_* — setup, muted, playing, broken-device, join-household...). Hardware capability flags adapt it to models with mic LEDs, mute LEDs, or only a status LED. SetLEDState's on/off is just the visible tip.
subsystems.log_domain_map: Every anacapa.*.log domain names a subsystem boundary — the 21 domains are effectively a module map of the binary. Useful when reading log output or /status pages.
subsystems.media_player_abstraction: Beneath AVTransport sits a plug-in layer of source implementations (media_player_mgr, autoplay, vli_ctrl, extaudiosrc, ai_impl_base) — each stream type (line-in, TV, Spotify, airplay...) plugs in through the same vtable. The action handlers you're using dispatch into this.
subsystems.model_sku_vocabulary: Model identifiers (ZPS9-ZPS61, S0-S9) and product names embedded for capability conditionals — which features a given hardware reports. The model→capability table hasn't been written out yet.
subsystems.multi_daemon_boundary: anacapad is one daemon of ~13 on the player. It pushes WiFi/network settings and PSKs to netstartd over /tmp/netstartd.ipc and receives connection-type updates back; LED, Bluetooth and power daemons get /X-external HTTP routes; each daemon has .dmp crash-report machinery. Most device behaviours (WiFi join, LED, BT pairing) are actually owned by the siblings.
subsystems.muse_semantics: The 'muse' API is Sonos's real product API — the REST-style surface the app talks to over the cloud/websocket channel. 525 routes are catalogued: every SOAP service is mirrored as an upnp* proxy (call + subscribe), and native namespaces cover players, groups, playback sessions, settings, home theater, alarms, timers, voice, trueplay/trueroom tuning, playlists, diagnostics and 'pinewood' remote control. Per-route request/response schemas remain the open work.
subsystems.play_history: Recently-played tracking: plays are recorded by the track monitor/recorder, buffered, and POSTed to the household history API with strict completeness rules; the app fetches an ETag-cached list; clearHistory/removeHistoryItem ops exist. Ratings (like/dislike) exist but only for the cloud queue.
subsystems.playlist_parsers: Below the URI layer sit real playlist parsers: ASX/WMP (mswmext), M3U (x-mpegurl), Apple HLS playlists (vnd.apple.mpegurl), DASH manifests. They turn playlist URLs into the track lists the queue consumes.
subsystems.qplay_protocol: Tencent's QPlay protocol (QQ音乐 casting). Only the QPlayAuth SOAP action is documented; the wider protocol — key derivation, the control channel, why it has a Control route but no Event route — is still undocumented.
subsystems.queue_persistence: How the queue survives reboots: saved queues are an XML document (.rsq) of SavedQueue+Track elements written atomically via a .tmp rename with a .d.rsq backup; the live queue persists as trackqueue.rsq; both are validated at boot and on replication. The SQ: object prefix exposes them to ContentDirectory and the SavedQueuesUpdateID variable tracks changes.
subsystems.runtime_flag_files: A set of sentinel files in /tmp and /var/run flip device behaviour at runtime: device_unlocked_flag, brokendevice, wifidisabled, crashed_play_state, event_preserve, wac_mode, netmanager_extender_flags, systemtimeoffset... They are the mechanism behind diagnostics, devmode and setup states.
subsystems.scrobbler: Last.fm scrobbling is built in: the player handshakes with post.audioscrobbler.com (Audioscrobbler protocol 1.2), then POSTs each played track as form fields (artist/title/timestamp/album/MBID...). On a BADTIME handshake it recovers by reading the HTTP Date: header. A newer ws.audioscrobbler.com/2.0 API is also linked. Which account it scrobbles for and the exact trigger policy are still unresolved.
subsystems.semisleep_power: A suspend/resume engine: featureConfigSemiSleep plus powerWakeupFromSemiSleep/AmplifierPowerStateChanged/DirectControlIsSuspended strings indicate players can enter a low-power 'semi sleep' and resume — relevant to idle latency and why a sleeping player can lag on first command. Not yet decoded.
subsystems.settings_replication: Household state is kept in sync by a replication protocol: each named store (accounts, netsettings, favourites, saved queues, areas) has a version+format handshake and per-item transfers between players; incompatible or malformed data gets the offending setting denylisted and the peer quarantined. This is why a setting changed on one player appears everywhere — and why joined players converge.
subsystems.sntp_server: Sonos runs its own time system: players sync from Sonos's *.sonostime.pool.ntp.org pool, but a single household player also hosts an SNTP server and the others sync from it — the server role can migrate. Grouped playback start times are scheduled on this clock, which is how multi-room audio stays in sample-accurate sync.
subsystems.spotify_esdk: A full embedded libspotify (the old Spotify eSDK — mercury/hermes protocol stack) lives in the binary, plus Sonos's bridge modules and mDNS Spotify-Connect discovery. This is the actual Spotify client implementation inside the speaker.
subsystems.telemetry_submission: The diagnostics pipeline: Telemetry 1.0 events tagged with field names, uploaded with the product-data-telemetry message-type header, plus the user-facing SubmitDiagnostics flow and a per-player positioning telemetry level setting. Several telemetry channels are individually feature-flagged.
subsystems.trueplay_tuning: Trueplay room tuning: the SOAP on/off surface is documented; the interesting parts — measurement capture, the tuning state machine, per-zone EQ application and the asset sync — are not yet decoded.
subsystems.update_machinery: Firmware updates are manifest-driven: a cloud manifest lists per-model target rows and a minimum auto-update version; household updates run check→download→launch across members with the coordinator orchestrating. Below the manifest's auto-update floor a device needs manual update. Clients see this through DeviceProperties/BeginSoftwareUpdate and the update/check muse route.
subsystems.wac_mode: WiFi Accessory Configuration — the Apple's-WAC-style setup mode where the player broadcasts a setup network (wacd daemon, /var/run/wac_mode flag, timeout). This is the first-boot/add-player path.
subsystems.device_unlock: A hidden developer-unlock feature: hitting /devunlock or /mfgunlock marks the player as unlocked (a flag file in /tmp) and reboots it. There's a server-side limit on how many times a unit can be unlocked, and diagnostic tests refuse to run on unlocked hardware — unlocked units are treated as non-production.
subsystems.testenv_environment: A hidden /testenv page lets a tester point the whole player at a different Sonos cloud environment (production, perf, staging, test or int) and override the update URL. It lists the six backend APIs the player will use, and the change spreads to every player in the household within about two minutes.

primitives.http_extra_endpoints: The complete inventory of HTTP paths the binary knows about beyond the SOAP control URLs — diagnostics, config pages, daemon IPC proxies, cloud-tunnel endpoints, media taps. Literal presence doesn't prove the route is registered at runtime, but the table shows the full attack/feature surface.
primitives.internal_result_namespace: The complete R_* status-code enum — 403 internal result codes grouped by family (account, cloud queue, playback ops, LED, masks...). These are what UPnP faults map FROM; the enum values themselves aren't recoverable as integers.
primitives.system_property_keys: The 29 R_* SystemProperties keys — the real key space that GetString/SetString/Remove operate on (crossfade duration, service bitrates, update policy, filtering).
primitives.smapi_capability_vocabulary: The full SMAPI capability flag vocabulary exposed by the /customsd form — auth types, container types and ~20 capability bits a music service can declare (favorites, extended metadata, device certs...).
primitives.csrf_protection: Browser-facing config endpoints embed a csrfToken hidden field, so simple cross-site form posts get rejected. If you're automating /advconfig or /status writes you must fetch the form first and echo the token.
primitives.device_description_variants: The two device-description XML variants — with and without AudioIn — proving AudioIn omission from some descriptions is deliberate.
primitives.gena_internals: GENA internals — SID preinstall (?sid=0), SubscribedEvents/LogicalSID/NotifyErrors bookkeeping, and the LastChange event assembly.
primitives.didl_classes_ext: The extended DIDL-Lite class vocabulary — audiobook/podcast/chapter object classes and playlist MIME types beyond the base UPnP set.
primitives.protocol_info_full: The verbatim GetProtocolInfo source CSV — every MIME/protocolInfo string the player claims to support, including x-rincon-* custom schemes, sonos.com-* types and DASH.
primitives.icy_metadata: ICY/Shoutcast metadata handling — icy-metaint interval parsing and stream-title extraction for internet radio.
primitives.alert_engine: The alert/chime engine — alertContent items (doorbell/voice-assistant prompts) play over or duck current audio per a priority policy.
primitives.household_psk_vocabulary: The household key hierarchy — HhPsk, ControlPsk, LanSwapPsk, RoomEncPsk and their backup slots: different keys for household membership, control channel, Wi-Fi roaming and room audio encryption.
primitives.replication_elements: The wire elements of household replication — ReplicationOperation/Player/Result triples plus Quarantined/Denylisted device records; the vocabulary of the sync protocol.
primitives.token_refresh_state_machine: The OAuth token lifecycle for cloud and music services — expiry detection, refresh requests, and retry/backoff behavior when refresh fails.
primitives.xml_schema_clusters: The recoverable XML schemas grouped by subsystem — settings stores, HT config, LED patterns, alarms — each element/attribute inventory with where it serializes.
primitives.internal_error_families: The internal error-code families — how component errors are namespaced before they get mapped to UPnP fault codes at the SOAP boundary.
primitives.http_status_endpoints: The player's built-in diagnostics website. Opening http://<player>:1400/status/ in a browser exposes ~63 pages of live internals — network stats, wireless scan results, CPU/thread info, settings stores, update state — plus passthroughs to shell commands (ifconfig, netstat, ps) and /proc files. It's the same tool Sonos support uses; some pages accept writes (setstring/removestring) so treat it as a control surface.
primitives.http_chunked_strictness: How strictly the player's HTTP parser enforces chunked transfer-encoding. Matters when a client sends unusual framing — the firmware rejects malformed chunk headers rather than guessing.
primitives.http_range: HTTP Range-request support — used for seeking in streams and resuming downloads. Defines which byte-range forms the embedded server accepts.
primitives.device_description_template: The XML template for the player's UPnP device description (what /xml/device_description.xml serves). Two variants exist — one including the AudioIn service and one without — so clients must not assume AudioIn is always advertised.
primitives.proprietary_headers: Custom HTTP headers the firmware emits and consumes — X-Sonos-* household/player identifiers, X-RINCON-BOOTSEQ boot-counter checks, the fake WMP NSS user-agent used when fetching Windows-media streams, and ICY metadata negotiation.
primitives.websocket_impl: The RFC6455 websocket stack shared by the local API (/api/v1/websocket, /websocket/api) and the cloud channel — opcode handling, per-message-deflate negotiation, ping/pong.
primitives.soap_fault_wire_format: The exact XML shape of a SOAP fault response from this firmware — the faultcode/faultstring/detail element layout a client must parse when an action fails.
primitives.soap_fault_code_vocabulary: Every UPnP error code the firmware can raise (UPnP-defined 4xx/5xx plus Sonos custom codes like ERROR_LASTFM_*), so clients can map numeric codes to causes.
primitives.soap_param_redaction: Parameters the firmware deliberately strips or masks in logging/diagnostics — mostly credentials and session tokens. If you see missing values in /status dumps, this is why.
primitives.soap_client: The outbound UPnP/SOAP client the player uses to call other players — coordinator-to-satellite calls, group joins, delegate actions all go through it.
primitives.gena_eventing: The UPnP GENA event layer: subscription tracking (SubscribedEvents, LogicalSID), SID preinstall for boot-time delivery, notify dispatch and per-service LastChange event variables. This is what delivers AVTransport/RenderingControl change events to subscribers.
primitives.upnp_eventing_impl: The concrete event-delivery machinery behind GENA — how LastChange blobs are assembled and pushed to subscribers' callback URLs.
primitives.upnp_client_stack: The player's UPnP control-point side — it acts as a client toward other Sonos devices (and historically other UPnP gear), handling M-SEARCH, subscriptions and action calls.
primitives.upnp_genaclient: The GENA subscription client — used when the player subscribes to another device's events rather than serving its own.
primitives.upnp_cloud_tunnel: The bridge that lets cloud/remote clients reach local UPnP actions — the upnp* muse namespaces tunnel through it, which is how the app controls a player it's not on the LAN with.
primitives.subscription_manager: Tracks active GENA subscriptions: who is subscribed to which service, renewal expiry, and cleanup when subscribers vanish.
primitives.ssdp_discovery: The SSDP responder/advertiser — answers M-SEARCH, announces the player on boot/network change. This is what makes the player discoverable at all.
primitives.ssdp_signed_msearch: Support for signed/authenticated M-SEARCH — discovery requests carrying credentials get different answers than anonymous ones.
primitives.mdns: The mDNS/Bonjour side of discovery — advertises Sonos services (and Spotify Connect presence) alongside SSDP.
primitives.dns_sd: DNS-SD service registration — the text records and service types published over mDNS.
primitives.discovery_layer: The combined discovery surface — SSDP + mDNS + Sonos's own peer-finding that builds the household picture.
primitives.target_udn_routing: How requests addressed to a specific player UDN get routed inside a grouped/bonded setup — a request can land on one member and be forwarded to the right zone player.
primitives.svcmanifest: The service manifest — the compiled table mapping UPnP service types to their control/event URLs and dispatch records.
primitives.svc_array: The flat service array the manifest is built from — every registered UPnP service with its handler pointers.
primitives.mega_impl_object: The mega-implementation object — many UPnP service interfaces share one underlying C++ object that fields calls for several services at once.
primitives.composite_subobject_interfaces: Some services expose nested implementation objects (e.g. line-in and HT-input sub-objects inside AudioIn) — the composite pattern used to share logic.
primitives.deviceproperties_impl_vtable: The DeviceProperties service implementation table — which function handles each action (GetZoneInfo, SetLEDState, AddBondedZones...).
primitives.audioin_impl: The AudioIn service implementation — line-in streaming control (StartTransmissionToGroup etc.), the deliberately-omitted-from-SCPD service.
primitives.device_auth: How the player authenticates itself and incoming calls — device certs, signed requests and the local-auth decision layer.
primitives.device_account_endpoint: The /device_account endpoint handling the player's account binding — links the hardware to a Sonos account.
primitives.device_registration: The registration flow — how a new or reset player registers with Sonos cloud and gets its identity.
primitives.cloud_registration: Cloud-side registration handshake — the player exchanging cert + household info for cloud credentials.
primitives.cert_identity: The certificate identities the player can present — the four client key/cert slots (Sonos, device, legacy-accept, registered-device) used for different peer classes.
primitives.auth_capability: The authentication capability bits — which auth methods (certs, tokens, household keys) a given peer/API accepts.
primitives.smapi_auth_policies: The per-music-service auth policy layer — maps each service's declared auth type (anonymous, userId, deviceLink, appLink) onto token storage and refresh.
primitives.service_accounts: Music-service account storage — per-service credentials, nicknames and tokens under SystemProperties; what AddAccount/DeleteAccount/RefreshAuthToken act on.
primitives.muse_authhelper: The auth helper shared by muse/websocket endpoints — checks tokens and household membership before a route handler runs.
primitives.noncehandler: The nonce challenge/response machinery — one-time values used to authenticate management operations.
primitives.audio_pipeline: The audio path inside the player — source → decode → DSP → output stages and the hooks between them.
primitives.audio_subsystem_files: The source-file layout of the audio stack (decoder, dfx, spdif, output stages) — useful as a map of which module owns what.
primitives.audio_clip: The alert/chime clip player — short audio files that interrupt or duck current playback (doorbell-style alerts, setup tones).
primitives.autoplay: Automatic source switching — when a TV powers up or a line-in gets signal, the player can switch to that source by itself; this is the logic that decides when.
primitives.extaudiosrc: External audio source abstraction — TV/HDMI, line-in and similar live sources are modeled through this interface.
primitives.chsnk_processor: CHSNK = channel-sink processing — the receiving side of Sonos's inter-player audio stream, jitter buffer and all.
primitives.ht_chsnk_processing: The home-theatre variant of channel-sink processing — satellites/surrounds receive their own audio channels over this path.
primitives.bt_sbc: Bluetooth SBC codec plumbing — present in the binary even on models without BT hardware; part of the shared codebase.
primitives.hdmi: HDMI/ARC/eARC input handling — TV audio ingest, CEC-adjacent control and the Dolby/DTS format negotiation.
primitives.sounddev: The sound-device layer — ALSA-ish abstraction over the DSP/codec hardware (tas5708 amp, TDM bus, SPDIF).
primitives.hls_radio: HLS support for internet radio — the firmware parses #EXTM3U playlists, picks variants, and recovers when a playlist goes empty.
primitives.smartplay: Sonos's 'SmartPlay' adaptive streaming — the bitrate/buffer logic that decides how aggressively to buffer and when to drop quality.
primitives.queue_engine: The playback queue engine — tracks, positions, shuffle/repeat state, and the URIs behind AddURI/RemoveTrackRange style actions.
primitives.queue_engine_object: The queue object's internal structure — the persisted form that becomes savedqueues.rsq.
primitives.cloudqueue: Cloud Queue support — services (Spotify etc.) push a track window to the cloud; the player loads it via loadCloudQueue[WithWindow] muse calls and pages windows as playback advances.
primitives.play_state_mgr: The per-zone play-state model — the state machine behind TRANSITIONING/PLAYING/PAUSED and how transport ops change it.
primitives.trackplaymonitor: The playback monitor that watches track progress — feeds play history, scrobbling triggers and completion stats.
primitives.content_managers: The per-source content managers — line-in, TV, library shares, streaming services each get a manager that normalizes them into the queue.
primitives.cd_object_resolver: The ContentDirectory object resolver — maps object IDs (FV:2, SQ:, R:0...) to the right store/browse handler.
primitives.media_player_mgr: The media-player manager — owns the active source player, autoplay policy and switching between local/cloud/external sources.
primitives.topology: The zone-group topology model — how the player sees the household: zones, coordinators, members, bonded pairs.
primitives.topology_engine: The engine that computes and applies topology changes — grouping, ungrouping, coordinator election.
primitives.group_coordination: Coordinator duties — the elected player runs the group's queue, volume-sync and event fan-out.
primitives.group_modes: Group operating modes — solo, stereo pair, bonded home theatre, satellite roles and what changes between them.
primitives.bonded_zones: Bonded-zone state — stereo pairs and SUB bonds are persistent pairings, not just grouping; this tracks them.
primitives.ht_bonded_zones: The home-theatre bonding variant — surrounds/SUB binding to a Playbar-class master, with role enums like HT_BONDED_SATELLITE.
primitives.avt_session_lock: AVTransport session locking — prevents two clients (or two group members) from fighting over transport control mid-operation.
primitives.persistent_stores: All the on-flash stores under /jffs — settings XML/JSON, saved queues, alarms, zones — their file names and formats.
primitives.device_state_store: The player's own state store — identity, registration, boot counters and flags.
primitives.alarm_store_object: The alarm store object — the in-memory model behind alarmclock.xml.
primitives.alarm_persist_writer: The writer that flushes alarm changes to flash — atomic write-then-rename so a crash mid-save doesn't corrupt alarms.
primitives.sp_store_object: SystemProperties store object — the key/value backing for GetString/SetString/Remove actions.
primitives.sqlite_timers: The SQLite-backed timer store (timer.db) — alarm/sleep timers with trigger times and a paused_timers table that freezes remaining_seconds + pause instant.
primitives.toml_config: TOML-format config parsing — used for some internal config files alongside XML/JSON.
primitives.xml_parser: The shared XML parser layer — used for DIDL, SCPD, settings XML and most of the schemas in this database.
primitives.sonos_concurrency: The threading primitives — mutex/condvar/thread wrappers the whole binary is built on.
primitives.sonos_libs: The internal support libraries — logging, strings, containers, time — the 'stdlib' layer under everything.
primitives.thread_inventory: Every named thread in the process — a map of what runs concurrently (eventing, streaming, control, cloud).
primitives.watchdog: The watchdog integration — threads must check in or the process gets SIGKILLed; /status/watchdogs exposes state, and debug/prevent_wdog_sigkill can disarm it for debugging.
primitives.healthcheck: The health-check machinery — self-tests the player runs and reports (linked from diagnostics).
primitives.diagnostics: The diagnostics bundle machinery — what /diag* and submitDiagnostics gather and where they send it.
primitives.diagnostic_manifest: The manifest listing which files/commands go into a diagnostic bundle.
primitives.devmode: Developer mode gate — /devmode toggle that unlocks extra diagnostics/config knobs on non-production units.
primitives.testenv_logger: Logging around environment switching — which cloud env the unit is pinned to and when it changed.
primitives.runtime_policy: RRuntimeZPPolicy — the runtime policy engine that combines local settings + entitlements to decide what features are on.
primitives.system_overrides: System override knobs — config values that change normal behavior for testing/recovery.
primitives.startup: Boot/startup sequencing — what anacapad initializes and in what order (source-file map of main path).
primitives.idle_events: Idle/timeout event handling — what fires when the player sits unused.
primitives.wake_on_lan: Wake-on-LAN support — the player can wake peers/be woken for coordinated power behavior.
primitives.internal_event_bus: The internal pub/sub bus — subsystems subscribe to events (topology change, settings change, button press) without calling each other directly.
primitives.hwmessagelib: The hardware-message layer — multicast BUTTON/AMP-style messages between players on the LAN.
primitives.hw_input_events: Hardware input events — button presses, IR, touch panels arrive through this layer before dispatch.
primitives.ir_remote: IR remote decoding — irdecoder + /jffs/irconfig.txt learned codes + the ir.ws.sonos.com code database.
primitives.component_map: The source-component map — the big table of *.cxx/*.c files embedded in the binary, grouped by subsystem.
primitives.linked_libraries: Shared libraries the binary links against — libsqlite3, curl, openssl et al., with versions where embedded.
primitives.circuitbreaker: Circuit-breaker pattern around outbound calls — failing cloud/peer endpoints get backed off instead of retried hot.
primitives.cloud_request: The generic cloud-request helper — HTTPS calls to Sonos APIs with cert pinning, env bases and retry policy.
primitives.muse_common: Shared muse-API plumbing — route table, JSON/request helpers, the layer every /api/v1 handler sits on.
primitives.pinewood_remote: A remote-control API: the pinewood muse namespace exposes TV-remote verbs — power, volume up/down, mute, dpad, back, home, settings, play — callable through the cloud. Likely used to relay remote commands to an attached TV or to drive a remote UI from the app.
primitives.migrationmanager: The migration manager — moves settings/data between software generations (e.g. favourite migration from old Rhapsody/OAuth formats).
primitives.usage_data_sharing: The telemetry consent layer — the opt-in/opt-out plumbing that gates product-data telemetry.
primitives.telemetry_pipeline: The telemetry upload pipeline — event buffering, X-Sonos-MessageType framing, submission scheduling.
primitives.reporting_policy: Which events get reported upstream and at what level — the policy knobs behind telemetry granularity.
primitives.spotify_esdk: The embedded Spotify stack — a full libspotify (mercury/hermes protocol) plus Connect mDNS/transfer support, an RSpotifyPlayback* control surface, its own track queue, and SMAPI position reporting.
primitives.location_engine: Location settings — the geo/region data that drives radio catalogs, available services and regulatory bits.
primitives.zone_experiments: The <ZoneExperiment> A/B store — replicated per-household experiment values with defaults, gated by featureConfigZoneExperiment.
primitives.wss_event_vocabulary: The vocabulary of events that flow over the websocket/cloud channel — the event types above the TLV framing.
primitives.native_protocols: Sonos's proprietary LAN protocols — SCI, MRPC, netstart2, TLV, CHSRC/CHSNK — the buses players use among themselves below UPnP.
primitives.wifi_hal: The Wi-Fi HAL — the driver-facing abstraction over the Atheros radio (ath_rincon /proc hooks).

primitives.netsettings_mgr: Network settings manager — the netsettings store pushed to/pulled from netstartd.
primitives.mdp_flash: Flash partition handling for MDP (media/data partition) versions — MDP2Ver/MDP3Ver fields in ZPInfo.
primitives.mod_zp: The mod_zp layer — zone-player module glue, likely the shared library boundary.
primitives.rmd_op_worker_class: The RMD operation worker — the worker-thread class that runs remote-management ops off the request thread.
primitives.timedjobs: The timed-job scheduler — Job* schema elements, deferred/recurring tasks the player runs.
primitives.timers: The generic timer wheel — underlies alarms, retries, keepalives.
primitives.dropout_logging: Dropout instrumentation — dropout_triggered status page + counters logging audio pipeline underruns.
primitives.tls_stack: The TLS stack — the OpenSSL-ish layer, cert verification modes and cipher handling for outbound HTTPS.
primitives.entitlements: Entitlements vocabulary-level record — see the entitlements subsystem entry for the decoded version.
primitives.audiotap: Debug audio taps — /audio_tap and /spdiftap endpoints capture raw audio sections to files for diagnosing lip-sync and dropouts; guarded, versioned file format.
primitives.location: Live location-settings changes — how a region change propagates (the /status page + settings store).
primitives.albumart_proxy: The player's album-art endpoint. Controllers are handed URIs like http://<player>:1400/getaa?u=<source-url>&v=<version> and the player fetches the image upstream and streams it back with a ~6-month Cache-Control header. Two things to know: 'u' must be the LAST parameter - the parser stops when it sees u=, so size flags (m=1 medium, s=1 small, vli=1 virtual-line-in art) only take effect if they come before it; and v= is never read by the server at all - it exists purely so you get a fresh URL when art changes. Requests are queued and served asynchronously; if you close the connection early the player detects it and discards the request. Upstream fetch failures come back as 404.
primitives.muse_route_verbs: The complete operation list of the muse (app/cloud) API: every resource and what you can call on it — playback controls, cloud-queue sessions, volume, groups, settings (in privilege tiers), home-theater accessories, Trueplay measurement sessions, alarms, timers, voice onboarding, remote control and diagnostics. It also exposes verbs for hardware this unit lacks (battery cells, water detection, PoE, ship mode), because the API surface is shared across the whole product line.

uri_formats.x-rincon-queue: How you address the local play queue: x-rincon-queue:<device> identifies a player's queue, and #<n> selects the 1-based track position. This is the URI you set as AVTransportURI to play a queue.

uri_formats.x-rincon-stream: The URI for room-to-room streaming — pointing a player at x-rincon-stream:<source> makes it play another player's audio (this is what line-in sharing and grouping use underneath).
uri_formats.x-rincon-mp3radio: The marker for plain internet radio MP3 streams — when a service hands a direct MP3 URL the player wraps it in this scheme.
uri_formats.x-rincon-playlist: URI for the player's built-in Sonos playlists (the saved 'Sonos Playlists' list), not to be confused with the playback queue.
uri_formats.x-rincon-cpcontainer: ContentDirectory provider containers — RDCPA:/RDCPI: variants address browsable music-service container roots.
uri_formats.x-rincon-buzzer: The built-in buzzer/alarm-tone URI — a local chime sound, usable as an alarm sound.
uri_formats.x-rincon-sonarcal: URIs for the sonar-calibration tones (leader/testtone/complete_ht .ogg) — played during Trueplay setup; not normal content.
uri_formats.x-rincon-configmode-sonar: Setup-mode tone URIs used while the player is in calibration/config mode.
uri_formats.x-sonos-vli: Virtual line-in — a URI that references another player's line-in as a source, the mechanism behind 'line-in sharing'.
uri_formats.x-sonos-misc: Assorted internal x-sonos-* schemes (HT audio stream, http wrappers, service markers) — mostly internal transport plumbing.
uri_formats.x-sonosapi-*: The cloud/music-service URI family — x-sonosapi-* URIs are content refs that resolve through Sonos cloud APIs rather than direct URLs.
uri_formats.x-sonosapi-radio: A Sonos Radio station URI: x-sonosapi-radio:ST:<id>?sid=&flags=&sn= — carries station id and flags for the radio service.
uri_formats.spotify_scheme: Spotify content URIs — spotify:track: / spotify:episode: plus the x-spotify:// transport wrapper used when the embedded Spotify client owns playback.
uri_formats.explore_scheme: explore:* container URIs — browsable 'explore' trees for services that expose them.
uri_formats.rdradio_scheme: rdradio: URIs select streaming-radio station sources.
uri_formats.hls_radio: Marker scheme for HLS-based internet radio streams.

uri_formats.pndrradioad: Pandora ad-insertion transport scheme — ad segments arrive as pndrradioad:// URIs.
uri_formats.skd: skd: — a streamer vocabulary token; semantics unresolved (plausibly a secure-key-delivery or SDK marker).
uri_formats.stub_scheme: stub: — a placeholder/no-op transport marker scheme.

uri_formats.oauth_jwt_urn: The standard OAuth JWT-bearer grant URN used in token exchange flows.

state_variables.RCS.SubGain: Sub output level — only on setups with a bonded Sub.
state_variables.RCS.AudioDelay: Lip-sync offset — delay applied to align audio with video.
state_variables.RCS.SonarEnabled: Whether Trueplay/sonar calibration is active on this player.
state_variables.RCS.PresetNameList: EQ preset names — includes 'FactoryDefaults' used by factory reset.

state_variables.CD.ContainerUpdateIDs: Per-container update ids — the standard UPnP change signal for browse caches.
state_variables.GRC.GroupVolume: The whole group's volume — settable only on the group coordinator.
